# dtcloud_vm_history (Data Source)

Lists what has been done to a virtual machine.

This is an event log rather than desired state, which is why it is a data source: there is nothing
to create, change or destroy.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "dtcloud_vm_history" "web" {
  vm_id = dtcloud_vm.web.id
}

# Newest first, so the first entry is the most recent action.
output "last_action" {
  value = data.dtcloud_vm_history.web.entries[0].activity
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `vm_id` (String) ID of the virtual machine.

### Read-Only

- `entries` (List of Object) Actions recorded against the VM, newest first as the API reports them. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--entries))
- `id` (String) The ID of this resource.

<a id="nestedatt--entries"></a>
### Nested Schema for `entries`

Read-Only:

- `activity` (String)
- `date_and_time` (String)
- `id` (String)
- `initiator` (String)

## Behaviour worth knowing

~> **Keep it out of resource arguments.** The content changes whenever anything happens to the
machine, Terraform's own changes included, so a resource that depends on it sees a new value on every
plan and never settles. Use it for outputs, for `terraform console`, or for a check outside the
dependency graph.

* **There is no `status` here.** The list endpoint leaves it out; `dtcloud_vm_history_entry` reads one
  entry in full.
